## Purpose

This note records the current empirical-model state after the July 2026
factor-of-two checks. It is deliberately scoped to points that affect how the
code should be read. More speculative mechanics arguments belong under the
explicit interpretation heading below.

## Current Code Behaviour

The active empirical model is `model_empirical` in `src/core/models.py`.

As of this note, the empirical model uses one shared slope scale,
`mu_emulator`, not separate `mu_emulator_v` and `mu_emulator_h` parameters.
The current configuration prior is in `configs/default_config.py`:

```python
"mu_emulator": {"mean": 0.0054, "scale": 0.001}
```

For each standard angle, the model samples angle factors centred on the load
components:

$$
\gamma_v(\alpha) \sim N(\cos\alpha, \sigma_{\gamma v}),
\qquad
\gamma_h(\alpha) \sim N(\sin\alpha, \sigma_{\gamma h}).
$$

The generated experiment-level slopes are currently:

$$
\beta_v = \mu_{\mathrm{emulator}}\gamma_v + b_i,
$$

$$
\beta_h = 2\mu_{\mathrm{emulator}}\gamma_h + b_i.
$$

The explicit factor `2.0` is therefore in the current code for the horizontal
shear-extension channel. The same additive experiment-specific slope bias
`b_i` is added to both normal and shear slopes when `add_bias_slope` is enabled.

The empirical likelihood currently observes the three DIC extensometer columns
as batched replicate curves. In code, each `(N, 3)` experimental extension array
is transposed to `(3, N)` and passed to a multivariate normal likelihood whose
mean is one load-extension curve. That is different from the diagnostic scripts
which often fit or plot the averaged DIC extension.

The full GP model path still has compatibility code for split
`mu_emulator_v`/`mu_emulator_h` if those keys are present in the configuration.
That is not the active empirical configuration described above.

## Observed Evidence

Origin-constrained regressions on the averaged experimental data, fitting only
the normal component and then predicting shear with the factor-two relation,
gave:

| Alpha | Fitted normal slope [mm/kN] | Predicted shear slope [mm/kN] | Observed shear slope [mm/kN] | Observed / predicted |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 45 | 0.003864 | 0.007729 | 0.007590 | 0.982 |
| 135 | -0.003786 | 0.007573 | 0.007881 | 1.041 |

The prediction used

$$
\beta_{h,\mathrm{pred}} = 2\beta_v\tan\alpha.
$$

The finite-element emulator training data also shows approximately the same
two-to-one direction effect when fitted against the corresponding load
components:

| Quantity | Slope [mm/kN] |
|---|---:|
| FE shear extension vs. \(P\sin\alpha\) | 0.01055 |
| FE normal extension vs. \(P\cos\alpha\) | 0.00520 |
| Ratio | 2.03 |

This means the factor-two pattern is present in both the experimental DIC data
and the FE emulator outputs. It is not only an experimental fitting artefact.

## FE And Experimental Extraction Difference

The FE extraction folder reviewed was:

```text
/Users/kai21/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-UniversityofBath/Mech Eng/OHT data (Tobi Laux)/MAF_lhs
```

The FE script `simulation_data_extract.m` performs rigid-motion correction and
then computes:

```matlab
disps_corr = (coords_1_corr - coords_0)/2;
```

It then extracts horizontal or vertical extension with the same
top-minus-bottom virtual extensometer function:

```matlab
extensions(i) = mean(disps_top) - mean(disps_bot);
```

The experimental extraction scripts reviewed use the same virtual extensometer
idea, but do not apply the `/2` before calculating extension:

```matlab
disp_corr = coords_1_corr - coords_0;
```

The `/2` in the FE extraction scales both FE shear and FE normal outputs. It
therefore does not explain the FE shear/normal ratio by itself. Removing it
would double both FE slopes while leaving their ratio essentially unchanged.

## E1 Sensitivity Of R(alpha)

The scalar reference compliance in `docs/empirical_model.qmd` is

$$
R(\alpha) = \frac{1000L}{A E_{\mathrm{eff}}(\alpha)}.
$$

Changing only \(E_1\) has almost no effect on \(R(\alpha)\) at 45 and 135
degrees under that off-axis formula. This was checked because different \(E_1\)
values have been discussed in the manuscript and project history.

| E1 [MPa] | R(2 deg) [mm/kN] | R(45 deg) [mm/kN] | R(90 deg) [mm/kN] | R(135 deg) [mm/kN] |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 145000 | 0.002269 | 0.023531 | 0.031014 | 0.023531 |
| 154900 | 0.002129 | 0.023519 | 0.031014 | 0.023519 |
| 161000 | 0.002051 | 0.023512 | 0.031014 | 0.023512 |

Relative to \(E_1 = 154900\) MPa, \(E_1 = 161000\) MPa changes \(R(45^\circ)\)
and \(R(135^\circ)\) by about -0.03 percent. \(E_1 = 145000\) MPa changes those
values by about +0.05 percent. The effect is only noticeable close to zero
degrees: \(R(2^\circ)\) changes by about -3.65 percent for 161000 MPa and
+6.58 percent for 145000 MPa.

## Interpretation

The strongest non-speculative statement is that the current factor-two empirical
form matches a pattern found in both experimental and FE-extracted extension
data.

A plausible mechanics interpretation is that the horizontal DIC
top-minus-bottom displacement difference is an engineering-shear-like
displacement measure rather than a tensor-shear strain measure. That would make
a factor of two mechanically plausible. This explanation is not stated
explicitly in the old manuscript versions or in the MATLAB extraction scripts,
so it should be treated as an interpretation to verify before using it as a
paper claim.

## Open Checks

- Decide whether the FE `/2` convention should remain as historical emulator
  provenance or be corrected in a future regenerated emulator dataset.
- Decide whether the empirical model should keep additive `b_i` slope bias or
  switch to a multiplicative specimen compliance factor such as
  \(\eta_i\), where \(\eta_i > 1\) means a more compliant specimen and
  \(\eta_i < 1\) means a stiffer specimen.
- Run and analyse a fresh explicit empirical MCMC bundle before treating this
  parameterisation as viable evidence.
